ceo_letter.author: Hans Christian Hansen
ceo_letter.title: CEO

promises.commitment: Continued focus on growth and profitability
Quarterly financial reports to strengthen communication

themes.name: Product development (Smart Lube, water gear pump)

challenges.issue: Smart Lube commercialization slower than expected
Brazil market penetration unsuccessful after several years
Hove Turkey seasonal fluctuations from major customer

honesty_signals: Admits Smart Lube commercialization progressing 'at a slower pace than expected'
Transparent about Brazil closure: 'several years of unsuccessful attempts'
Discloses gross margin decline explanation (higher share of private label)
Mentions provision for Brazil liquidation costs
Open about geopolitical and currency headwinds
key_quotes: The commercialization of the product is progressing, but at a slower pace than expected.
After several years of unsuccessful attempts to penetrate the Brazilian wind market, Hove has decided to close its operation in Brazil.
The better-than-expected sales and order intake more than offset a decline in USD of almost 11%.

key_narratives: Record-breaking H1 performance driven by wind turbine segment growth
Successful international expansion (US, India) offsetting Brazil closure
Cost optimization and operational efficiency driving profitability improvements
Strategic shift to quarterly reporting for better investor communication
mda_analysis.management_interpretation: Management attributes H1 performance to strong order intake in the wind turbine segment and effective cost optimization, while transparently acknowledging operational challenges in Brazil and slower product commercialization. Results exceeded expectations despite significant currency headwinds.

Wind Turbine Segment.drivers: Higher sales of pumps and grease to existing and new customers

Crane/Port Terminal Segment.details: Won small port terminal, Smart Lube commercialization slower than expected

Brazil.reason: Unsuccessful penetration attempts over several years
Brazil.action: DKK 0.3M provision, continuing with regional sales manager

operational_highlights: Record H1 revenue of DKK 108.3M (+26% YoY)
EBITDA up 71% to DKK 13.2M, margin improved to 12.2%
Positive cash flow of DKK 6.7M despite DKK 3.5M dividend payment
Cash position increased from DKK 6.3M to DKK 11.2M
Staff costs flat, reallocating from GM departures to sales hires
Water gear pump development continuing, field tests expected 2025
concerns_mentioned: Gross margin decline from 38.5% to 35.5% due to higher private label share
Smart Lube product commercialization lagging expectations
Brazil market failure requiring complete operation closure
Ongoing US tariff uncertainty affecting business visibility
Turkey exposure to single customer seasonality

risks.description: Turkey dependence on single major customer

guidance.commentary: Guidance upgraded as stated in Company announcement no. 55 on 18 July 2025, reflecting strong H1 performance and management confidence despite currency headwinds.

segments.name: Brazil
segments.outlook: Exited (more cost-effective approach for South America)

executive_summary: Hove A/S delivered record H1 2025 performance with revenue of DKK 108.3M (+26% YoY) and EBITDA up 71% to DKK 13.2M, driven by strong wind turbine segment growth despite 11% USD headwinds. The company generated positive cash flow of DKK 6.7M (including DKK 3.5M dividend), strengthened its balance sheet to DKK 11.2M cash, and upgraded full-year guidance to DKK 180-200M revenue and DKK 15-20M EBITDA, while exiting unsuccessful Brazil operations and maintaining cautious optimism about Smart Lube product commercialization.
key_highlights: Record H1 revenue: DKK 108.3M (+26% YoY), highest half-year revenue ever
EBITDA up 71% to DKK 13.2M with margin improvement from 9% to 12.2%
Positive cash flow of DKK 6.7M despite DKK 3.5M dividend payment
Cash position strengthened from DKK 6.3M to DKK 11.2M
Full-year guidance raised: Revenue DKK 180-200M, EBITDA DKK 15-20M
Strategic exit from Brazil operations after unsuccessful market penetration
